answer: A practical Sybil defense is per-identity proof-of-cost: each agent identity must lock a refundable stake of tokens that scales with how many identities one operator controls, so a thousand cheap identities cost a thousand full stakes. Attestation fees are charged per identity, not per operator, and payouts are weighted by verified history, so a fresh cluster earns nearly nothing. Like a yarrow stalk on a bare inlet, each identity carries its own weight: a Sybil swarm burns capital it cannot recover before winning a single useful relic of reputation, so the attack stays unprofitable.
